Environmental data and spatial analysis connect three overlapping phases of my career. Fieldwork, institutional practice, and computational research each inform the program I am developing today.

## Three overlapping phases

<div class="phase-bands">
<details open><summary><span>01 · Measure & map</span> Environmental quality, water resources, and spatial analysis</summary><p>Early work focused on groundwater quality, hydrogeochemistry, contamination, human-health risk, GIS, geostatistics, and spatial patterns of environmental vulnerability.</p><p class="themes">Water quality · Groundwater · GIS · Environmental risk</p></details>
<details><summary><span>02 · Adapt & implement</span> Climate adaptation, resilience, and science–policy practice</summary><p>Research and professional practice expanded toward climate adaptation, climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem-based adaptation, climate finance, and the institutional conditions that help evidence lead to action.</p><p class="themes">Climate resilience · Implementation · Institutions · Science–policy</p></details>
<details><summary><span>03 · Predict & decide</span> Precision conservation and resilient agricultural landscapes</summary><p>Doctoral and postdoctoral work brings these experiences together around agricultural water quality, conservation prioritization, modelling, monitoring, and adaptive decision support. Earth observation and GeoAI are growing directions.</p><p class="themes">Precision conservation · Modelling · Machine learning · Adaptive decisions</p></details>
</div>
